Title: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Nalbuphine ER Tablets for Uremic Pruritus
Author: Mathur et al.
Comment: The paper reports a 0–10 NRS, not literally a VAS. M_diff is the paper's adjusted least-squares mean difference from the MMRM, while group means/SDs are raw changes. test_statistic was derived as M_diff/SE_diff = -0.73/0.31 because no t value was reported. Table 2 arm Ns were used, although the text reports 371 evaluated for efficacy and elsewhere defines an MITT population of 369. Shared placebo arm must not be double-counted if both doses enter one meta-analysis.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Nalbuphine ER 120 mg BID') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Phase 2/3 multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel-group trial
Study Environment: 41 United States investigative sites and 6 investigative sites in Romania and Poland
Medium: Nalbuphine extended-release tablets or matching placebo tablets
Content length: 8 weeks of treatment; evaluation period was treatment weeks 7 and 8
Topic of Content: Kappa-opioid agonist therapy for uremic pruritus
interaction_type: Patient-reported worst daytime and nighttime itching collected during dialysis visits
Participant type: Hemodialysis patients with moderate or severe uremic pruritus
Outcome measurement: Change from baseline in Worst Itching Intensity NRS, 0 (no itching) to 10 (worst possible itching)

Title: κ-Opioid System in Uremic Pruritus: Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Studies
Author: Wikström et al.
Comment: Only the eligible parallel-group Study 1 week-4 result was extracted; Study 2 and paper-level pooled/sensitivity analyses were excluded because they involve a crossover design. Table 1 values are reported in mm on a 0–100 VAS. For the planned 0–10 cm synthesis, divide means, SDs, M_diff, and SE_diff by 10. M_diff was computed as placebo minus nalfurafine (52.6 − 40.3 = 12.3 mm), so a positive value favors nalfurafine. SE_diff was computed from the explicitly reported SDs and Ns as sqrt(27.8^2/26 + 24.0^2/25) = 7.264 mm. The paper does not report a Study 1 week-4 P value or CI; the narrative only says statistical significance was not demonstrated.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Nalfurafine 5 μg') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel-group clinical trial
Study Environment: Multicenter hemodialysis settings in Sweden, Denmark, Norway, and Finland
Topic of Content: Treatment of uremic pruritus with nalfurafine
Participant type: Adults with ESRD undergoing routine hemodialysis and experiencing severe uncontrolled uremic pruritus
Outcome measurement: Self-evaluated worst itching during the previous 12 hours on a VAS from 0 mm (no itching) to 100 mm (worst itching ever)
effect_direction: Lower pruritus severity is better; a negative treatment-minus-placebo mean difference favors treatment.

Report_ID: Change from baseline at week 8 in weekly mean of daily 24-hour WI-NRS score
Title: Randomized Controlled Trial of Difelikefalin for Chronic Pruritus in Hemodialysis Patients
Author: Fishbane et al.
Comment: The paper reports an adjusted mixed-effects repeated-measures analysis using LS mean changes and SEMs, not raw change-score means and SDs. The outcome is explicitly a 0–10 WI-NRS rather than being labeled a VAS. The pooled active group is the paper's prespecified combination of all three difelikefalin dose arms. Negative values favor difelikefalin because lower itch severity is better.
Design Type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, four-arm parallel-group phase 2 trial; mixed-effects model with repeated measures
Medium: Intravenous study drug administered after hemodialysis
Topic of Content: Treatment of moderate-to-severe chronic kidney disease–associated pruritus
interaction_type: Difelikefalin or placebo administered after each hemodialysis session three times weekly
Participant type: Adults undergoing hemodialysis with moderate-to-severe chronic kidney disease–associated pruritus
Outcome measurement: Patient-reported 11-point WI-NRS recorded daily; weekly mean analyzed, with higher scores indicating worse itch intensity
Outcome variable: Change from baseline at week 8 in weekly mean of daily 24-hour WI-NRS score
effect_direction: Lower pruritus severity is better; a more negative treatment-minus-placebo change difference favors treatment.

Report_ID: Change from baseline in mean VAS value during the latter 7 days of treatment
Title: Effect of a novel kappa-receptor agonist, nalfurafine hydrochloride, on severe itch in 337 haemodialysis patients: a Phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
Author: Kumagai et al.
Comment: The reported values are ANCOVA-adjusted least-squares mean decreases, not raw post-treatment means. Larger positive change means greater itch reduction. No SD or SE is reported, so none was inferred. The shared placebo arm must not be counted twice when combining the two active doses. Values are retained verbatim in mm on the explicitly stated 0–100 mm VAS; numerically divide by 10 only during synthesis to express the effect on a 0–10 cm scale.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Nalfurafine hydrochloride 5 μg') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA: missing F-value or group sizes
Design Type: Phase III randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial
Participant type: Haemodialysis patients with severe itch resistant to currently available treatments
Outcome measurement: Adjusted least-squares mean decrease from the last 7 days of pre-observation to the latter 7 days of treatment
Outcome variable: Change from baseline in mean VAS value during the latter 7 days of treatment
effect_direction: Lower pruritus severity is better; because the paper reports decreases, a larger positive decrease favors treatment, equivalent to a negative treatment-minus-placebo change in severity.

Report_ID: Mean change from baseline in weekly mean WI-NRS score at week 12
Title: A Phase 3 Trial of Difelikefalin in Hemodialysis Patients with Pruritus
Author: Fishbane et al.
Comment: The paper used the WI-NRS (an 11-point numerical rating scale from 0 to 10), not a scale explicitly labeled as a 0–10 cm VAS. Figure 2 graphically presents least-squares mean changes and SE bars, but the supplied text does not state their numerical values. No values were estimated from the image; therefore means, SEs/SDs, and mean difference are null, and this report cannot contribute numerically to the planned MD meta-analysis without verified figure data or supplementary numerical results.; unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 trial
domain: Uremic pruritus / chronic kidney disease–associated pruritus
Topic of Content: Difelikefalin treatment for moderate-to-severe pruritus in adults undergoing hemodialysis
Participant type: Adults undergoing hemodialysis with moderate-to-severe chronic kidney disease–associated pruritus
Recruitment source: 56 trial sites in the United States
Outcome measurement: Least-squares mean change from baseline in weekly mean WI-NRS score at week 12, analyzed using a mixed-effects model with repeated measures
Outcome variable: Mean change from baseline in weekly mean WI-NRS score at week 12
